title: Multi-Cloud Security Posture (CSPM) Findings

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `(sourcetype=aws:securityhub OR sourcetype=azure:defender OR sourcetype=gcp:scc)` into `index=security`. Confirm UC-4.4.6 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `(sourcetype=aws:securityhub OR sourcetype=azure:defender OR sourcetype=gcp:scc)`. Confirm UC-4.4.6 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=security` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via Splunk TAs for each cloud, or CSPM product integration (e.g. Prisma Cloud, Wiz); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Splunk TAs for each cloud, or CSPM product integration (e.g. Prisma Cloud, Wiz)
spl:
index=security sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (sourcetype=aws:securityhub OR sourcetype=azure:defender OR sourcetype=gcp:scc)
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.6_multi_cloud_security_pos_6"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.4.6 — Multi-Cloud Security Posture (CSPM) Findings: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:cloudtrail` for search criteria `(sourcetype=aws:securityhub OR sourcetype=azure:defender OR sourcetype=gcp:scc)` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), detecting 'Multi-Cloud Security Posture (CSPM) Findings' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.6 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Ingest Security Hub, Defender for Cloud, and SCC findings into a common index. Normalize severity and finding type. Alert on new critical/high. Dashboard open findings by cloud, severity, and category (e.g. encryption, networking).
visualization: Table (cloud, severity, type, count), Bar chart (findings by cloud), Trend line (findings over time).
knownFalsePositives: A fresh scanner run or a vendor re-rate can resurface a finding we already know about. We deduplicate on resource and time and we only escalate when the exposure is new or the severity stepped up.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=security`.
• Install and configure Splunk TAs for each cloud, or CSPM product integration (e.g. Prisma Cloud, Wiz) with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest Security Hub, Defender for Cloud, and SCC findings into a common index. Normalize severity and finding type. Alert on new critical/high. Dashboard open findings by cloud, severity, and category (e.g. encryption, networking).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=security sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=security sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (sourcetype=aws:securityhub OR sourcetype=azure:defender OR sourcetype=gcp:scc)
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.6_multi_cloud_security_pos_6"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=security` to detect multi-cloud security posture (cspm) findings. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_6_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (cloud, severity, type, count), Bar chart (findings by cloud), Trend line (findings over time)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk TAs for each cloud, or CSPM product integration (e.g. Prisma Cloud, Wiz) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of multi-cloud security posture (cspm) findings so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
